component.name: Bible Corner - KJT
component.summary: Holy Bible and the Orthodox faith

description.p: Bible Corner - KJT (Knowing Jesus Today) is a Bible reader for Linux: read the Holy Bible with the Orthodox faith, study it with the Holy Fathers, and keep it all on your computer, to read also without the internet.

ul.li: The Holy Bible in many languages, with search, comparison, cross-references and the Greek and Hebrew words
The Holy Fathers beside every chapter, and their writings to read like books, by topic and by era
Bookmarks, colours, notes and Study Pads, kept in step with your phone and the website when you sign in
A library of free Bibles, commentaries, dictionaries and books from CrossWire and AndBible, the Septuagint and the Church Fathers first
The Bible Maps in the land's real colours, with story maps such as the journeys of St Paul
Today with God: the verse of the day, the feasts, the saints and the readings of the day
Share a verse as a picture, with your own photo if you like

description.p: Everything you choose to download is kept on your computer.

description.p: A bookmark of several verses opens in the Bible with all its verses chosen, and its bar shows the whole passage (John 3:16–17), its Study Pads and its note.

Churches near me: the directory now loads even when the website refuses apps its files (it comes through the app's own address), and a map picture that fails no longer stops it. My churches: star a church to keep it at the top of the page and on the map, every time.
Six new app icons to choose from in Settings › App icon: Gold, Royal blue, Royal purple, Blue, Teal and gold, and Violet.

Reading pages easy on the eyes (Settings › Reading page): Cream paper, Old book, Warm peach, Evening sepia, and Candlelight for a dark room. A new Settings page and an Offline library that shows clearly what is on this computer, with Delete. Directions to churches (by car, on foot, by bike), and the church directory says what went wrong if it cannot be reached. Recordings now play for the CrossWire King James Version. Games are bigger, with sounds and full screen. A coloured world map with capitals under the Bible maps. Easier-to-read People and places. In Arabic the whole app now reads from right to left, more of the app is translated, dates are in your language, and after changing the language a Restart now button shows every page in it.

Export your study from My Study: a file for AndBible (your bookmarks, notes and Study Pads, added to what AndBible already has, nothing replaced), or a KJT JSON backup to restore here or on the website.

Prayer, Good Fun and Churches near me are now made by the app itself, not the website in a frame. Prayer: the daily prayers, the Creed and a poem; ask for prayer; the prayer board, to pray for one another and reply (what you write without internet is sent later). Churches near me: search a town, a postcode or a church name, or press Near me (your computer asks you first); the Orthodox churches and monasteries by distance, on a map. Good Fun: Sudoku, Word Seek, Bible Crossword, Who Am I?, Memory Match, Books of the Bible, Bible Timeline and Verse Builder, with trophies and your best scores; more games are coming.

You Today, as in the Android app: choose how you feel and read what God says to you in the Scriptures (in your language, kept on this computer). Prayer, Good Fun and Churches near me open inside the app. Study Journey is third in the menu. Listening: the chapter now scrolls with the verse being read. The arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Space scroll the chapter. Compare with up to four Bibles, each named under the verse, and the compare button shows which ones are on. A bookmark takes the colours of its Study Pads (in several pads, several colours), or no colours if you switch them off; the Study Pads are right in the bar under the chosen verses.
Safety: your sign-in on this computer is kept readable by you alone.

Listening follows the reading: the verse being read glows and the chapter scrolls with it (switch it off with Follow along). A fuller player: previous and next verse or chapter, a seek bar, speed, a sleep timer, keep listening into the next chapter, "Listen from here" from any verse, and keep a chapter or a whole book on this computer. The Orthodox calendar on Today with God: any day, the great feasts marked. Long lists can be folded: Bibles in other languages in Downloads, and each kind in the Library. In the menu: the pages of the website (Prayer, You Today, Good Fun, Churches near me) and Report a problem.

Listening: the King James Bible now plays with music, as on the website and the phone. The player shows "With music" or "Reading only"; your choice is remembered, and chapters kept on this computer are kept for each recording.

Now called Bible Corner - KJT, like the Android app. Bible Study Journey, as in the Android app: your reading journey (the whole Bible chapter by chapter, books, milestones, reading plans of the Church, streaks, the prayer before reading) beside My Study; "Mark as read" under every chapter (or automatically), kept in step with your account on the website and the phone.

Light or dark: a button at the top of the sidebar, and Appearance in the menu (follow the computer, light or dark). The sun on Today with God is now a plain "Today" button, shown only on another day. The icons of the great feasts (old icons, public domain) on Today with God. The grammar of each Greek and Hebrew word (STEPBible). In Russian: the Philokalia (St Theophan the Recluse) and the Lives of the Saints (St Dimitry of Rostov) in the Holy Fathers. More of the app in the nine languages. A day with a coming feast no longer stops Today with God.

A new icon, and five to choose from (Downloads and language › App icon): purple, navy blue, black, green and wine red, the same as the Android app. The History books have a clearer colour in the book list.
More of the app in the nine languages: Downloads and language, My Study, the Library and Today with God.

The app's menus in the nine languages of the website. Bible Maps: old Bible atlases (maps engraved centuries ago, public domain) to open and zoom, kept once opened; the map data corrected (the figurative Babylons of 1 Peter and Revelation were pinned on Rome, and more): the names of one spot now share one pin. Library: search inside a whole commentary, book or dictionary. The Holy Fathers by author, A to Z. SimpleX first: talk to us on SimpleX from the menu, and the daily verse post for the website's administrators, to SimpleX and Telegram. The Android app is one click away in the menu.

Long Bible names are cut short at the top. The highlight colours always fit the window (on their own line when there is little room). My Study: on a wide window the bookmarks are a table with the Bible, the Study Pads, the date made and the date changed; on a narrower one these show under each bookmark. New sorting: by Study Pad and by Bible.
Sign in with your study key, as on the website (or with a name and password).

The Holy Fathers as on the website: read by topic, in coloured tiles (Prayer, Repentance, the Mother of God …); the Fathers in their eras, each era in its own colour, with the topics they wrote on; the topics of each writing; and a search.

My Study in two columns: the Study Pads on the left, the bookmarks and notes beside them, each scrolling on its own (drag the line between them to change their widths). Every page now fits medium and small windows: the small-screen layout follows the room the pages really have.
Choose several verses as on the website: click the first, then the last. “+ Next verse” and “− One less” now sit beside the verse reference. The last chosen verse is always fully highlighted.
The first click after opening the app or a chapter chooses one verse, instead of selecting half the page; the page no longer slides to the end of the text when you click into it.

A Library: the free Bibles, commentaries, dictionaries and books of CrossWire and AndBible, the Orthodox ones first (the Septuagint, St John Chrysostom, the Early Church Fathers, the Didache). You see the list first and choose; each is then read without the internet. A Bible from the Library becomes one of your Bibles; the commentaries show beside the Holy Fathers in the reader. A click always chooses one verse, even a shaky one. Study Pads in coloured cards, with their own colours and emoji, and their bookmarks highlighted in the pad's colour. The maps: the rest of the world (countries and today's capitals), a scale ruler, slower zoom, All places and Story maps as on the website. Side panels can be made wider or narrower by dragging their edge. Today with God can be shared as a picture or as text.

A new app icon. Choosing verses is steady: a click chooses one verse; Shift+click (or "Next verse too") makes a range; Ctrl+click adds one verse. Share a verse as a picture, as on the website: eight looks or your own photo from this computer, four shapes, three kinds of letters; copy it or save it. Study Pads show by their names, not as tags, and a new Study Pad is made with its own name. Edit a bookmark in one place: its colour, note and Study Pads. In My Study, fold the Study Pads and the bookmarks away, sort them (Bible order, newest, oldest, last changed, colour), rename a Study Pad, and edit each bookmark.

Like the website reader: tap a verse, then another, to choose everything between them (or choose "from verse … to verse" in the book picker), then bookmark, highlight or write a note on the whole range. Above each chapter: your notes and bookmarks in it (with Next), the people and places named in it, and the Holy Fathers on it. Notes show as one short line under their verse; click to read or edit the whole note.

Clearer bookmarks: the bar shows what a verse already has (bookmark, colour, note, Study Pads); remove a bookmark or its colour, edit or delete a note, and undo each change. Downloads in a queue, two at a time, each with its own progress, to stop or try again. Book names follow the language of the Bible being read. The app's language follows the computer unless chosen. The Orthodox cross drawn the right way.
Steadier: right click (or a long press) chooses the verse and shows the one action bar, now with words beside its icons; the maps use less memory; if the app ever freezes, a small log shows where.

A richer reader: it always opens on the Holy Bible and offers to continue at the very verse where you stopped; choose a book, a chapter and a verse; books coloured by their kind with a legend; right click (or a long press) on a verse for everything you can do with it; cross-references; the Greek and Hebrew words with their meanings; the words of Christ in red; your notes under their verses; the people and places of each chapter.
Faster, simpler and more modern: its own icons, smooth maps, pages that open at once, downloads four files at a time, and a layout that fits small screens and phones.
A new app, made for the computer: no web pages any more. Signing in to My KJT works in the app.
